summary.headline: Chambal Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 12% to INR 851 crore on 17% margin despite revenue falling 12% to INR 5,000 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations fell about 12% YoY to INR 5,000 crore as urea volumes dropped on the bunched Gadepan-1 and extended Gadepan-2 shutdowns and complex fertilizer placement was measured. EBITDA rose 12% to INR 851 crore with margin expanding about 350 bps to 17%, and PAT grew 10% to INR 703 crore. Management attributed margin gains to Gadepan-3 urea economics, a currency tailwind, some ammonia sales and advance NPK purchases. Management said the company is preparing for a possible fourth urea plant under the National Investment Policy for Urea 2026, with a Board decision pending.

financial_highlights.change: market debtors INR 841 crore; subsidy receivables INR 2,460 crore

financial_highlights.value: USD 17.25 per unit for the quarter

segments.name: Urea
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,860 crore vs INR 3,109 crore, down 8% on lower production and sales from shutdowns; management said profitability remained healthy. Gadepan-3 was the main margin driver.

segments.name: Complex fertilizers (NPK)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,737 crore vs INR 2,131 crore, down 18% on measured placement during delayed sowing; segment EBIT rose 67% to ~INR 239 crore, helped by earlier advance NPK purchases.

segments.name: Crop protection, specialty nutrients and seeds
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR 430 crore vs INR 458 crore, down 6% on deferred farmer purchases; segment EBIT rose 13% to INR 108 crore with margin ~25%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 to progress well as sowing catches up and channel liquidation creates second-round demand; July urea farmer sales ~380,000 t and NPK ~92,000-93,000 t.
NPK margins expected to decline as purchase prices average out, though a certain level will be maintained.
Technical Ammonium Nitrate: management expects a better season from early October (Q3); marketing mix and warehousing expected complete by end-December.
New urea plant (~1.27 million t G3-type capacity discussed): financial bids expected by about mid-October, then Board approval; commissioning indicatively within 2030.
IMACID phosphoric acid capacity expansion from 500,000 t to 700,000 t expected operational around April-June 2027.
Dividend to be maintained at about 25% payout; buyback not on the horizon unless no project visibility.
capex_capacity: Potential fourth urea plant under National Investment Policy for Urea 2026, estimated near INR 10,000 crore (management cited INR 9,000 crore brownfield case in Q&A); Board approval pending.
Management cited EBITDA of around INR 12,000 per tonne for the new urea plant at steady state, against ~INR 13,500 per tonne product price assumption.

TAN project: weak nitric acid and ammonium nitrate solution production started; ammonium nitrate melt trial production from ~15 June; high-density AN nearing commissioning. Sales made but not booked in P&L; proceeds decapitalised the project until commissioning is formally complete.
Q1 AN sales split: G1 ~96,000 t, G2 ~1.85 lakh t, G3 ~3.29 lakh t.
CFCL-TERI Centre of Excellence lab operational; new products expected from FY28-29.
demand_pricing: Industry offtake was subdued early in Kharif: summer crop sowing ~183 lakh ha at end-June, ~23% lower YoY; acreage reportedly caught up by late July after July monsoon revival.
Raw material costs (ammonia, sulphur, phosphatic intermediates) rose sharply on West Asia disruption; prices eased toward quarter-end but remained above historical levels.
Kharif NBS subsidy revised up ~10% but set before the price spike; NPK subsidy announcement delayed, and management expects action around October.
Chambal holds ~8.5-9 lakh t of NPK tied up with vendors for the season; mgmt said it bought advance inventory from January.
Consumption ~404-405 lakh t vs production ~305-306 lakh t, per management.
TAN realisations currently above budgeted margins per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is a fresh application needed for the new urea plant, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the application window is open and a bank guarantee process follows government approval; financial bids should be available by around mid-October, after which Board approval is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Can full G3 capacity be utilised by November?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the plant's maximum run rate is about 9.5-10 lakh t, so the policy-period quantity cannot be completed in time.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the complex fertilizer margin jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Advance NPK purchases made earlier, flagged in the previous call, allowed placement at better margins; management expects margins to decline as prices average out.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new policy return-dilutive versus NUP-2012, and what is the gain-sharing structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the policy is dilutive versus the prior one, citing scale and single-site benefits. The 12%-16% ROE band is indicative with a gas price range of USD 6.5-14; efficiency gains beyond it are not capped, and no gain sharing applies up to eight years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for TAN utilisation and oversupply risk, including Reliance's entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees a possible slight oversupply for about a year, then demand exceeding supply again; it sees no utilisation problem and said Reliance's plans are too speculative to assess.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend and buyback policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend to be maintained at about 25% payout; buyback not planned unless project visibility is lacking.

risks_watch: Subsidy disbursement and NPK subsidy revision timing; receivables of INR 3,300 crore including INR 2,460 crore subsidy receivables.
Gadepan-1 and Gadepan-2 shutdown durations and urea volume recovery.
Sulphur supply and price for IMACID; the JV resumed production in July after a temporary shutdown.
Gas price (provisional USD 17.25 in Q1) and currency movement, which management cited as margin drivers.
Urea policy classification for the existing NIP-2012 plants, which expires by December; government data review is ongoing.
TAN market oversupply risk and potential entry by Reliance; capex cost discipline on the proposed urea plant.
Tape and e-token distribution restrictions; a state suspended its e-token system after agitation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and the long-term urea opportunity, but cautious on subsidy timing and raw material costs. Management was direct on margin tailwinds and policy dilution, and gave concrete numbers on monsoon-led offtake. Answers on the new urea plant's cost and timing were more qualitative and deferred to Board approval.
key_quotes: Despite the bunched shutdown and an extended period of Gadepan-1 shutdown, we did deliver INR 2,860 crores, against INR 3,109 crores, lower by 8% due to lower production and sales.
Backed by a strong balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation, we remain well-positioned to create sustainable long-term value for our stakeholders.
So, that means the pickup is close to 19,000-20,000 tons a day, which is quite good in terms of how things are improving.
But the advantages of scale at a single place have to be also factored in, when you were to analyze the entire edifice of this policy.
I think dividend, whatever numbers I have done, we will definitely maintain the numbers that we have got.

growth.why: No numeric revenue growth guidance; Q1 revenue fell ~12% on urea shutdowns and NPK placement, with EBITDA up 12% on Gadepan-3 economics and NPK inventory gains. Growth rests on IMACID expansion (500k to 700k t, ~Apr-Jun 2027), TAN commissioning and a possible fourth urea plant (~INR 10,000 cr) still awaiting Board approval, with management guiding NPK margins lower and urea capped at 9.5-10 lakh t
